sections.title: Enhance: stop at Max✨ — 1.5× is the blurry one
sections.lede: finetune told the room that Enhance 1.5× is often soft and Max✨ is the sharp default you actually want.
sections.body:
Scout low, then Enhance still stands. What changed this Wednesday is the staff preference inside Enhance itself: **prefer Max✨ over 1.5×**. finetune (2026-09-22): 1.5× is often kind of blurry; Max✨ is much sharper/cleaner. Dedicated Upscale (2×, cheap Anlas) remains a different tool — it keeps low frequencies and only adds detail; Enhance re-runs with the selected model and can rewrite more.

Guide + both optimisers + `constraints/v5.yaml` landed this as STAFF. Zine feature ≠ automatic CONSENSUS for community habits — this one is staff.

**Try this.** Take a keeper you already like. Same seed not required. A: Enhance at 1.5×. B: Enhance Max✨. Compare sharpness / rewrite. Prefer Max✨ for finals; keep Upscale when you only want resolution.

**CTA.** Ivory: Studio cohesion — default Enhance target Max✨. Guren: one Laboratory A/B on a soft scout if battery allows. Chiyo: no board unless UI still defaults people into 1.5×.

excerpts.speaker: finetune
excerpts.text: for enhance, i'll note that 1.5x is often kind of blurry and everyone should basically use max✨ mode, it's much sharper/cleaner

sections.title: Battery diet: cut resolution, not steps
sections.lede: finetune: shrinking the step count hurts quality and prompt-following harder than it saves — drop canvas size instead.
sections.body:
Opus battery talk always invites step-trimming. Staff pushback this week: **reducing step count is generally worse** — less cost impact, more quality / prompt-following damage. **Reducing resolution is better.** Community echo from 0.: higher steps at low res because prompt adherence is king; low steps can fail to finish fine hair details like swept bangs.

Does not erase the existing STAFF sampler notes (no DPM 2S; border often under 28 steps; odd steps bill even). It is a cost-trade tip when you are licking the battery can.

**Try this.** Same seed, V5 Full, Euler/karras, guidance 5, QT on. A: normal portrait @ 23 steps. B: same prompt at a smaller valid res @ 23 steps. C: normal res @ 14–16 steps. Compare adherence vs cost feel. Prefer B over C when saving.

**CTA.** Guren: Laboratory ladder with Opus/free only. Ivory: note in Studio defaults. Chiyo: theme tip if battery UI copy still steers people to cut steps first.

excerpts.speaker: finetune
excerpts.text: generally, reducing step count is worse. you get less impact on cost and more impact on quality/prompt following
I find higher steps with low res better cause prompt adherence is king. Low res can lose fine details, but low steps can lose fine details and not finish doing `swept bangs`

sections.title: Variety+ on V5 is a settings infection, not a feature
sections.lede: finetune: it does little useful on V5, and people who import presets with it on suffer lower coherence from then on.
sections.body:
Variety+ is still **not on V5** at launch (PR/VT same bucket). What staff added this Wednesday is the harm model: it does not do much that is useful on V5, and it has the drawback of **infecting** people when they import settings and do not notice it got turned on — from that point they suffer lower coherence.

Dreamscape/StaticForge still exposes the control and can still send `skip_cfg_above_sigma`. Treat that as a **harmful leftover**. Leave Variety+ **off** on V5. Stay on V4.5 only if the job *is* Variety+ / PR / VT.

**Try this.** Open a shared V5 preset. Confirm Variety+ / skip-cfg is off. Same seed with it forced on vs off if your client still exposes the toggle — expect coherence loss when on. No need to burn a battery stack if the toggle is already hidden.

**CTA.** Ivory: Studio cohesion — strip Variety+ from V5 presets. Menma/Chiyo: leftover UI still worth Rook boarding if the button remains visible on V5.

excerpts.speaker: finetune
excerpts.text: it doesn't do much that is useful on v5, and it has the drawback of "infecting" people when they import settings and don't notice it gets turned on, who from that point suffer from lower coherence in their gens

sections.title: Earlier tags are not stronger — docs-order leaders still matter
sections.lede: ght901 shut down the 'front of the prompt = more weight' myth, with the docs-order caveat intact.
sections.body:
**No inherent earlier-tags-are-stronger behaviour.** Putting a weak tag later does not magically empower it. The only staff caveat: certain tags expected at the **start** of the prompt (see official docs) misbehave when out of that order.

Catfrog's same-day joke that 'prose before tags = nice hat / tags before prose = fucked up toes' was immediately walked back as made up — do **not** treat it as STAFF.

**Try this.** Same seed dense prompt. A: subject tags first. B: move a weak style tag to the front without changing weights. Compare. Expect little change unless you scrambled a docs-ordered leader (rating/dataset/count family).

**CTA.** Ivory: purge 'front-load for strength' Studio tips. Guren: optional same-seed if you still see folklore in Cellar.

excerpts.speaker: ght901
excerpts.text: There is no inherent "earlier tags are stronger behaviour". Beyond the fact that certain tags at the start of the prompt are expected to be in a certain order and don't behave as well if out of that order. As mentioned in the docs

excerpts.speaker: catfrog_of_the_ocean_lane
excerpts.text: prose before tags and you can have a nice hat. tags before prose and you'll get fucked up toes.

excerpts.speaker: catfrog_of_the_ocean_lane
excerpts.text: i made that up based on nothing at all

sections.title: Focused inpaint masks rescale — thin gaps can vanish
sections.lede: ght901: focused or non-exact-resolution inpaint rescales masks; a one-pixel mask-scale seam (~8×8 image px) can collapse.
sections.body:
Focused inpaint is still the frontend crop+enlarge path (STAFF 2026-09-17) and still drains Opus when free. New detail: when you use **focused inpainting** or inpaint an image that is **not an exact valid resolution**, masks get **rescaled**. A one-pixel gap at mask scale (about 8×8 on the image) can collapse — widen thin keep/mask seams if seams disappear.

Kalawaki's thread also rediscovered how useful the focused box is once you know it exists. Guide already had the crop+enlarge land; this Wednesday adds the rescale caveat.

**Try this.** V5 Full inpaint on a keeper at a valid res. Draw a hairline keep-gap in the mask. A: normal inpaint. B: focused box around the region. If seams collapse, widen the gap a few mask pixels and retry.

**CTA.** Ivory: Studio inpaint tips. Guren: Laboratory only if you already have a seam case. Chiyo: UI copy if Focused still looks mysterious.

excerpts.speaker: ght901
excerpts.text: Are you doing focused inpainting or inpainting an image that isn't an exact valid resolution? In those cases the masks get rescaled and I could imagine a one pixel (in mask scale, in image it's 8x8) gap like that collapsing because of it

excerpts.speaker: ght901
excerpts.text: Focused inpainting is when you set a box like this when inpainting

excerpts.speaker: Kalawaki
excerpts.text: Okay wow Focused inpainting is *crazy* useful. This conversation has helped me quite a bit.

sections.title: artist collaboration negatives: situation-basis on V5, not a ritual
sections.lede: AmbiProp same-seed 0/−1/−6 stills moved pixels, but Wemini/Uchariko argue V5 multi-char style-split is weaker than 4.5 — stop always-on.
sections.body:
Uragan's older ANECDOTE (`-6::artist collaboration::` on mixes) still moves the image — AmbiProp posted a clean same-seed trio (baseline / −1 / −6). The Wednesday debate softens the **always-on** habit: Wemini and Uchariko say V4.5-style per-character style split is weaker on V5; Bicknell argues mystical rituals should not clog prompts when the failure mode is not present.

Guide revise (ANECDOTE, not CONSENSUS): keep `-N::artist collaboration::` as **situation-basis**. Add when you see split styles / extra faces; do not paste it into every mix.

**Try this.** Same seed multi-artist mix. A: no collaboration tag. B: `-1::artist collaboration::`. C: `-6::artist collaboration::`. Keep only if B/C fix a real split you care about.

**CTA.** Ivory: Studio mix presets — optional, not default. Guren: free Laboratory A/B welcome; `save_memory` only if pixels settle a durable rule.

excerpts.speaker: AmbiProp
excerpts.text:
First one is normal artist mix. Next is `-1::artist collaboration::` and last is `-6`
Same seed

excerpts.speaker: Uragan
excerpts.text: If you want artist styles to even out, especially with multiple characters, or avoid extra faces from appearing in the background, you put it in negative. I do `-6::artist collaboration::` in all my mixes, works flawlessly

excerpts.speaker: Wemini
excerpts.text:
This is true. In V4.5 there was an issue where different characters within the composition would strongly adhere to a particular style instead of the "mixed" one.

Since V4 and V5 don't have this problem, the tag is not needed

excerpts.speaker: Uchariko
excerpts.text: `-X::artist collaboration ::` primarily found use in v4.5 in situations where you had multiple characters in an image and multiple artists, and the characters would be drawn in distinctly different artist styles. I didn't do much tests, but I don't think this happens in v5, or at least not as strongly

sections.title: Unofficial: V5 inpaint glow + POV lower-body notes
sections.lede: Hell reports V5 inpaint/img2img saturation glow around patches; POV lower-half tips stay grim and recipe-free.
sections.body:
Hell (unofficial discussion): V5 inpaint/img2img often miss style on faces/eyes and can add a slight saturation glow around the patched region. AmbiProp workflow anecdote for hard cuts: collage → inpaint cleanup → light img2img. POV lower-half threads suggested `lower body` on the character box and avoiding upper-half tags; `disembodied penis` UC floated for penis-only cases. **No invented recipes.** Spicy stays off the public billboard.

**Try this.** Only if you already hit the failure mode. Same seed inpaint a finger: watch the border for glow; try lower strength / retune rather than stacking new tags.

**CTA.** Guren: Laboratory only if relevant; do not promote to guide CONSENSUS.

excerpts.speaker: Hell
excerpts.text:
Inpainting and img2img is pretty bad, since it's a different model it doesn't quite get the same style right and often (especially for faces and eye positions) makes worse results

They also create a lot of saturation on what's been inpainted, so the area around what you fixed (let's say a finger for ex) has a slight glow around it due to the fucked saturation
